newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: POLL-Filinvest 6-mth net seen up 16.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Filinvest 6-mth net seen up 16.8 pct.

text.p: Robust demand for housing would help Filinvest Land Inc (FLI) post a steady growth in the first half of this year, despite problems with a major project and funding delays for the housing sector, analysts said on Monday.

The average of a Reuters poll of stock brokerages forecast Filinvest Land to post a recurring net profit of 1.18 billion pesos ($44.87 million) in the first six months, 16.8 percent higher than the year-earlier 1.01 billion pesos.
In the first three months, the firm made a net income of 404 million pesos, up from the recurring income of 277 million pesos in the same period last year.
For the whole of 1997, Filinvest Land would have regular net income of 2.53 billion pesos on average, a 25.2 percent rise from 2.02 billion pesos in 1996, the poll showed.

An extraordinary gain of 300 to 400 million pesos is expected this year from the recent sale of its 16 percent stake in Bonifacio Land Corp, the developer of a 214-hectare land at the edge of the financial district of Makati, analysts said.
Strong housing demand will underpin Filinvest's income stream, even though earnings are not expected this year from its new 677-hectare Sky City development project located east of Manila.

The firm's target sales of 21,000 low-cost housing units in 1997 comprise only 9.5 percent of the projected demand of 220,000 units and require only three billion pesos in funding, an ING Baring Securities study said.
Filinvest Land's Sky City project was put on hold by the government because of alleged breaches of environmental regulations. The company has appealed.
The first phase of Sky City, which covers the golf course, would have been launched in October this year.

"While environmental issues do delay the Sky City development, the impact on our forecasts is minimal. Sky City's contribution for this year is only four percent," said Rachel Evangelista, analyst of All Asia Capital and Trust Corp.

But one analyst said he had downgraded his forecast for the firm. "We originally projected 2.5 billion pesos (for Filinvest Land). But because of the problems with Sky City, it's now down to 2.3 billion pesos," said the analyst from Asia Equity.
Analysts said Filinvest had been less vulnerable to the effects of delayed funding from the government's home lending programme because it was not its key source of funding.
The government programme has had difficulty in releasing funds on time due to bureaucratic delays.

"FLI is well-poised to become a dominant player in the affordable housing market on the back of its low-cost land bank, strategically located projects and proven track record," the ING Barings Securities study said.

"Moreover, we expect buyers to become very selective in their purchases, choosing quality projects that have achieved critical mass which FLI can easily offer due to its vast inventory of over 30 projects," it said. Filinvest Land Inc results forecast: (figures in billions of pesos)
